analysis.title: GS - Mourad, Miller - Midterms - 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: With under a week to the midterms, the GS FICC & Equities desk says the more actionable question is which policy areas become easier to negotiate, get more regulatory attention, or gain leverage in future spending debates, rather than which Democratic priorities become law.
The House passed a continuing resolution funding the government through December 11 in a bipartisan vote, avoiding a shutdown into November.
Affordability is a common theme across Democratic and Republican agendas. The desk maps it to ACA subsidies, drug pricing, power costs and government spending.

ACA: the enhanced premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025, followed by premium increases and lower marketplace participation. Restoring them would likely return patient volumes to providers, who now see rising bad debt and uncompensated care. The desk is long its ACA-exposed beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA), recently rebalanced.

Drug pricing: both parties prioritize expanded Medicare negotiation, Most-Favored-Nation benchmark pricing, a redefined exclusivity clock, and stricter Medicaid and PBM obligations. The desk is short its drug-makers basket (GSHLCBPH).

Democrats would likely raise the number of drugs selected for negotiation each year beyond the 20 scheduled for 2029. MRK and AMGN have identified drugs that could face price setting from 2028, with projected US sales declines. Legislation tying US prices to international benchmarks would be 'drastic and unprecedented' per ALGS filings.

Power inflation: the desk calls datacenter power costs possibly one of the more underappreciated election-sensitive themes in US equities. The debate is shifting from whether datacenters get built to who pays for the added generation and transmission.

The desk is long Renewables (GSXURNEW), Grid Infrastructure (GSXUGRID) and Power Up America (GSENEPOW), and recommends buying protection on Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and Datacenter Equipment (GSTMTDAT). Polling shows datacenter concern is bipartisan but stronger among Democrats.

Government spending: Congress has run on continuing resolutions since the end of the Biden administration. Republicans want more defense spending without matching increases elsewhere, while Democrats want parity. The desk sees scope for debate on broader spending to pick up before November and around the December CR expiry.

The desk is long government-spending-exposed ex-defense and drug-makers (GSXUGOVT, recently rebalanced) and short defense spending beneficiaries (GSXUDFNS). Likely beneficiaries are domestic government contractors, federal agency suppliers, grant recipients and research institutions.

Corporate tax: the 2025 OBBBA made 100% bonus depreciation and other TCJA business provisions permanent, alongside the permanent 21% statutory rate. Because the President can still veto, the midterms are unlikely to change tax law. The desk sees 2027-28 earnings as largely insulated under either outcome, with the risk to valuations beyond 2029.

Antitrust: Democratic leaders have criticized current antitrust enforcement, and the desk sees potential for stricter Big Tech oversight. It cites past settlements (Live Nation/Ticketmaster, Nexstar/Tegna, Netflix/Paramount/Warner Bros) and says short Big Tech.

Financial regulation: Democrats have focused on rebuilding CFPB authority and Wall Street oversight. A less favorable regulatory backdrop could dampen bullish momentum in Financials. The desk says short Investment Banks and crypto-exposed equities.

Tariffs: investors should not assume meaningful relief. Democrats have limited ability to reverse tariffs while the President can use alternative authorities after the Supreme Court invalidated the IEEPA tariffs. The desk sees more risk of tariffs rising than falling between now and early 2027, and says short tariff-sensitive equities.

Housing: Congress passed bipartisan housing-supply legislation in 2026. Democrats could differentiate through expanded housing tax credits and first-time homebuyer incentives, though large fiscal measures need presidential approval. The desk says long Homebuilders.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats could gain agenda and oversight control, helping ACA-exposed providers, grid and renewables names, non-defense government spending and homebuilders.
tension_points.bear_case: Presidential veto limits legislation, and tariffs may rise. Big Tech, financials, drug-makers and datacenter-linked hyperscalers face more regulatory scrutiny or cost-bearing pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic win of the House or Senate that fails to lead to the oversight and spending leverage described, or a presidential veto on housing or tax measures.
